excerpt: Nuclear beta decay involves the conversion of one nucleon into another.

reviewedMappings.2026-3-10:0: For ordinary single beta-minus/plus decays excluding electron capture as specified, one nucleon converts into the other. A unchanged, Z changes ±1 and N changes ∓1; only statement 5 false.
reviewedMappings.2026-3-10:1: Beta-minus charge balance: 0=1−1+0; beta-plus in nucleus: 1=0+1+0. Total charge conserved including emitted lepton.
reviewedMappings.2026-3-10:2: Reviewed section expressly describes emission of electron or positron with antineutrino or neutrino and creation during decay, not release of pre-existing nuclear electrons.
reviewedMappings.2026-3-10:3: One nucleon converts into another; nuclear equations preserve A, the total neutron plus proton number.
reviewedMappings.2026-3-10:4: n→p in beta-minus increases Z by 1; p→n in beta-plus decreases Z by 1.
reviewedMappings.2026-3-10:5: At fixed A and N=A−Z, Z±1 necessarily means N∓1. Same-neutron-number claim is false.
